name: Use of sizeof() on a Pointer Type
principle: Code uses sizeof() on a pointer when it needs the size of the pointed-to object or array. This computes pointer width instead of data size, causing undersized buffers or partial comparisons.
detection_signals: malloc(sizeof(ptr)) where ptr has type T *
calloc(n, sizeof(ptr)) where ptr has type T *
realloc(ptr, count * sizeof(ptr)) where ptr has type T *
memcpy(dst, src, sizeof(ptr)) or memset(dst, 0, sizeof(ptr)) where ptr has type T *
strncmp(a, b, sizeof(ptr)) or memcmp(a, b, sizeof(ptr)) where ptr has type char * or void *
sizeof(param) inside a function where param is declared T param[] or T *param
new char[sizeof(ptr)] or new T[sizeof(ptr)] where ptr is a pointer variable
negative_signals: sizeof(*ptr) used for one pointed-to element
sizeof(ptr[0]) used for one pointed-to element
sizeof(array) where array is declared as T array[N] in the same scope
sizeof(void *) or sizeof(char *) used only in static_assert, logging, or platform word-size calculation
allocation uses count * sizeof(*ptr) with overflow-checked count
false_defense_traps: Casting malloc result, e.g. (T *)malloc(sizeof(ptr)), does not fix the size calculation
Using sizeof(param) on an array parameter still returns pointer size
Assuming pointer size equals element size on the current platform is non-portable
Replacing sizeof(ptr) with strlen(ptr) is wrong for binary buffers or missing terminators
verification_focus: Is sizeof() applied to a pointer in a context that needs the size of the referenced object, array, or full comparison length?

consequence_chains.trigger: pointer size is smaller than required object or array size during allocation/copy
consequence_chains.consequence: undersized buffer followed by out-of-bounds write or memory corruption

consequence_chains.trigger: sizeof(pointer) limits strncmp/memcmp authentication checks to pointer width
consequence_chains.consequence: partial credential comparison permits improper authentication

patch_principle: Use sizeof(*ptr) or sizeof ptr[0] for the pointed-to element size
Track array length separately; do not derive dynamic allocation size from a pointer
For buffers, compute count * sizeof(*ptr) and check multiplication overflow
Use explicit expected lengths for strncmp, memcmp, memcpy, and memset
